page.layout: One printed page: a centred heading "LECTORI." at the top, then one column of running text with a large woodcut initial at the start of the first paragraph. No margin notes, no running head, no page number.

main_text.head: LECTORI.
main_text.p: LECTOR candide, Orationes no-stras, quas in vrbe hac scripsi-mus jam olim, vt diuersas, ita &dissimiles nonnunquam, neque semel typis hactenus descriptas, uno hoc volumine cum editura olim essent operæ, perlegimus & emendauimus. Inprimis autem hac editione quæ nunc prodit, quam non paucis locis ita recensuimus, vt alia videri possit: ne nunc dicam, auctiorem esse. In ipsis autem, aut pro tempore, aut occasione, sæpe & imitatione autorum veterum, à quorum lectione ac studio recentes tum eramus, formam non eandem nec vbique similem secuti sumus. quæ in iis vt non una, ita neque omnes eadem delectat. Quibusdam enim copia & circumductionum grauitas diffusa, quæ verborum ambitu instructa, qualis dominascitur sic fertur, & torrentis instar auditorem secum rapit, mascula, robusta, ardens etiam si sit necesse ac concitata, tantum placet. In quo solus prope Tullius regnauit: scriptor vt eximius, ita fere ab omnibus

page.notes: The woodcut initial "E" is ornamental and is read as E. Words such as "Lector", "scripsimus", "diuersas" and others are printed with long-s and f-like forms in the scan; they are given in plain s. The final line "nibus" is printed in a catchword-like position at the right but is part of the sentence "ab omnibus", so it is kept in the text. Paragraph-initial words in italics are reproduced in italic type.
